claim: ONE FIX with VAL-R5-03 (V07). Two binding texts written this round give two outcomes for a crossing station that a carried-down raised way holds on the town enceinte that becomes the village palisade. §2.7's support step (3) (l. 2560-2564), from R5-02's held-stretch clause, reads: '`wallToWay`, `absorbWall` (§4.11; V06 §3.7.6 (5)) and the hand-off down that makes the enceinte the village's palisade (V07 §3.5a (4)) each leave it standing as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, with no gate law and no junction with a ring road'. V07 §3.12 (l. 2610-2615) says 'the standing fabric survives unchanged' and makes the palisade 'the innermost standing enceinte'. V07 §3.5a (4) (l. 1611-1614), from VAL-R4-03's amended text, keeps the station in the palisade's line, 'its support the band's stretch under the deck … with its raised gate whose tower carries the deck … — the one gate at a support the palisade carries'. T-V7-48 counts that raised gate among the palisade's gates at supports. Under the base, the tower stands outside the gate law. Under V07, it is a gate of the palisade. The palisade's gate set feeds VS3 step 7's split, F-V-GATE ('a trace with no gate after VS4'), the siege's engines facing 'then the gates', `gatesAndKeep`'s 'the palisade's gates' and the crisis look's gate-passage keep-out (§10.2 (d); T-V7-69 (b)). So two builders build two outcomes. §2.7 (3)'s list is right for `wallToWay` and `absorbWall`, where the wall line goes; at the hand-off down the line stays.
required_change: §2.7's support step (3): replace 'and `wallToWay`, `absorbWall` (§4.11; V06 §3.7.6 (5)) and the hand-off down that makes the enceinte the village's palisade (V07 §3.5a (4)) each leave it standing as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, with no gate law and no junction with a ring road, the enceinte's record kept while it stands' with 'and `wallToWay` and `absorbWall` (§4.11; V06 §3.7.6 (5)) each leave it standing as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, with no gate law and no junction with a ring road, the enceinte's record kept while it stands; the hand-off down that makes the enceinte the village's palisade keeps it in the palisade's line as the standing fabric it is (V07 §3.12) — a raised gate the one gate at a support the palisade carries, an aqueduct's arch no gate (V07 §3.5a (4))'. In the same step's parenthesis, replace 'a stretch laid after it — a village palisade's among them — takes no station' with 'a stretch laid after it — a village palisade VS3 lays after it among them — takes no station'. V07's side is VAL-R5-03.

claim: MATRIX-GAP (the arch vault's door under a later wall), verdict undefined. repair-r5-V04's HAND-OFFS (l. 103-111) put this question to the adjudicator, and no unit closed it. §2.7's support step (6) (d) (l. 2606-2608) has a wall stretch laid after a raised way end 'at a `vault` span … at its arch vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole'. V07 §3.5a (4) (l. 1607) and T-V7-48 say the same of the palisade. 'A walled-up arch' is V04's own term for an arch vault with no door (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1): 'no door is made and `W_ARCH_VAULT_NO_DOOR` is reported (a walled-up arch)'). Yet V04 keeps the vault's one `door` at the midpoint of an open face. Its two open faces are the grade faces that take a seated building's entrance and windows (§3.5.4 (f); V03 §3.12 (9)). No reconcile runs for a later wall, since a later trace changes no `feet`, `supports` or `spans` (R5-02), and T-V4-63 now bars 'no arch vault changed by either'. The trace crosses both mouths, so wherever it crosses near mid-span the run's end meets the face over the door. This is common at CITY, where a later stage's ring meets an S4 viaduct whose spans inside the town are `land` vaults. Nothing states whether the door stays, moves or is walled up, or what it opens onto. One builder walls up both mouths, leaving the vault and any building seated in it unreachable; another keeps a door that opens into the wall's masonry. Principle (11) grades an undefined edge on a normal path as major.
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (d): replace 'at a `vault` span ending at its arch vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole' with 'at a `vault` span ending against its arch vault's two open faces (V04 §3.5.4 (f)), the chamber kept whole with its door — where the run's end would meet the door's face over the door, the door moves along that face to the nearest point clear of the run's band, in the commit that lays the stretch (a fate in a hand edit's dry run), and keeps opening onto the ground beyond it; the far face is closed by the run's other end —'. V04's END: (1) §3.5.4 (d) (1)'s door rule adds 'a door that a wall stretch laid after the raised way would cover moves along its face to the nearest point clear of the run's band (§2.7's support step (6) (d)), the chamber, its key and footprint unchanged; with no clear point on either face, no door, `W_ARCH_VAULT_NO_DOOR`'. (2) `ArchVaults.reconcile`'s trigger lists (§1b l. 328, §2.6's arch-vault row l. 867, §4.3's row l. 2577) add 'a wall stretch laid across a `vault` span's strip (its door only)'. (3) T-V4-63's 'no arch vault changed by either' becomes 'no arch vault's key, footprint or closure changed by either, its door moved clear of the run where the run met it', and its fixture's circuit crosses the `vault` span at its door. V07's END: §3.5a (4)'s 'at an arch vault ending at its two walled-up arch mouths' becomes 'at an arch vault ending against its two open faces, its door kept clear (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. If the adjudicator rules instead that the mouths are walled up and the door removed, V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1) and (f) and T-V4-63 must say so in the same words.

claim: §2.7's support step (7) (l. 2623-2628, new this round, R5-02 (7)) 'keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position and support `ring` — and every span between two of them as it stands (`use`, `reason`, `state`, `held`)', then runs '(1)–(5) and the span rule … on the extension alone, from the old deck's last interior station (with none, from its other foot) to the deck's new end on the new ring'. So the old end span — from the last interior station to the ring-end foot, or a one-span deck's only span — is laid again, and it and every span beyond come out of the span rule with no `state` (standing): the old end span's `state` and its `held` `use` are not carried, nor (the kept list naming key, position and ring) a station's support `state`. V06 raises a fallen span only by `repairRaised` on a generated way 'whose reason is live again' (V06 §3.19.2 (5)), a declared way 'breaks only by a hazard or the landfall, and the user repairs it by hand' (§3.19.2 (1), item 101 R13), and `spans[].held` is 'an input override every regeneration keeps (§7.2)' (l. 2293-2294). An aqueduct sourced beyond the frame — the common ring-end foot (`RaisedFoot` l. 2312-2318) — whose end span its lapse, a topple or a landfall ruined before an epoch's rung crossing grows the frame has that arch stand again and a standing extension laid on a lapsed deck, with no repair, reason or event naming it; a user's held `use` on that span is re-ruled away. One builder follows (7) literally, another carries the end span's condition onto the extension (and keeps or resets a station's `state`): two behaviours, and no bar runs a frame growth over a fallen or held end span (T110-2's frame-growth clause and T-V4-65 run a standing aqueduct). VV34-r5-02 (V04, minor) notes the same re-laid end span for T-V4-63's vault wording only; one fix may close both.
required_change: §2.7's support step (7): 'keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position and support `ring` —' → 'keeps every station of the old deck — its key, position, support `ring` and `state` —'; after '…its stations' keys minted after the largest the way has held ((5))' add '; the deck's condition at the old ring carries over: each span the extension lays takes the old end span's `state` (a `ruined` or `cleared` end span leaving each new span `ruined` or `cleared`, so only a repair raises it — V06 §3.19.2 (5)'s for a generated way, a hand Repair for a declared one, V06 §3.19.2 (1)) and, where that span's `use` was `held`, the same `use` held (an input override the extension keeps as a regeneration does, §7.2), its new supports standing (supports outlast spans, V06 §3.19.2 (3)); with no interior station, the one old span is that end span'. `RaisedFoot`'s comment '(the old deck's stations kept, the support step's (7))' and §4.11's frame batches 'the old deck's stations kept (§2.7's support step (7))' each read 'the old deck's stations kept and its end span's condition carried (§2.7's support step (7))'. END under V06: §3.19's lead '(§3.2 (9), the old deck's stations kept, §2.7's support step (7))' → '(§3.2 (9), the old deck's stations kept and its end span's condition carried, §2.7's support step (7))'. END under scope: T110-2's frame-growth clause, after 'every station of the old deck at its key, position and ring after the growth (§2.7's support step (7))', adds 'and, on the same aqueduct with its end span on the old ring `ruined` by its lapse and, on a second run, with that span's `use` held by a user's `setAttr`, every span the extension lays `ruined` and, on the second run, carrying the held `use` — no fallen arch standing again and no hold lost'.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-history). A wall run laid after a raised way, when a part it was built against goes. §2.7's support step (6) (d) (base l.2603-2616) builds a later wall run against the raised way. 'each part of the reservation standing in its band is taken into the line, the run abutting its faces and closed against it'; 'at a vault span ending at its arch vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole'; and 'beneath every other span ... an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit (... derived at read ...)'. Its readers say the same: V06 §3.7.6 (5), T110-2 (4), V07 §3.5a (4), §8.4 (l.13672-13673, l.13897-13898) and §11.1's glTF and CityJSON rows (l.15988-15989), 'a run beneath a raised way's span topped at its soffit'. Nothing states what the run is once those parts go, and every one of them can go after the run is laid. V06 §3.19.2 (3) dismantles a support whose spans have fallen, leaving it cleared (V06 l.2925-2931); only a crossing station is spared, and a support a later wall abuts is no station. (4)'s topple takes a support. A vault span's breach collapses its arch-vault chamber 'in the same batch' (l.2932-2934), and that chamber was the part 'closing the line' between the run's two ends. A span falls ruined or cleared, so its soffit no longer exists, though §8.4 and §11.1 still cap the run at 'a raised way's span'. A hand delete of the raised way removes its vaults in the same commit (T-V4-63). So the wall line is left with a gap - a pier's width, or a whole span's length where a vault stood - or with a run capped under a deck that no longer exists. One builder leaves a gap in the enceinte (its barrier closure broken with no breach recorded); another closes it; another keeps the cap. The path is normal in long histories: H-AQUA's epoch circuit runs beneath its standing aqueduct (T-V6-47), and an aqueduct that runs dry lapses, falls by span and is salvaged (V06 §3.19.2 (2)-(3)). V07 defines the village case only at the next derivation (T-V7-48). No bar runs the town case.
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (d), after '...`bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line at a hand edit's dry run).', add: 'What such a run is built against is read from the reservation as it stands - a support whose state is absent or ruined, a ramp, stair or foot of a standing raised way, a vault span whose state is absent with its arch vault - and its soffit cap from a span whose state is absent, both derived at read, never stored: where a part goes after the run was laid - a support cleared (V06 §3.19.2 (3)) or toppled (V06 §3.19.2 (4)), a vault span breached and its chamber collapsed with it, a span ruined or cleared, the raised way deleted or suppressed - the run stands whole across that part's former footprint and to its full height beneath the fallen span, in its own condition and material (its trace never left its course), with no gap and no op; its setback, glacis and berm stay as S7 cut them until the run is next re-traced (§7.3's S7 row).' (The adjudicator may instead rule the former footprint a breached run, provided the op removing the part is named as its one writer and the same bar runs it.) Ends: (1) rendering: §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF and CityJSON rows, 'a run beneath a raised way's span topped at its soffit' -> 'a run beneath a raised way's standing span (its state absent) topped at its soffit'. (2) V06: §3.19.2 (3)'s support and span bullets and (4)'s topple add 'a wall run laid after the way and built against what falls standing whole across its footprint (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. (3) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (4) adds 'and, after its epoch circuit ran beneath the standing aqueduct, that aqueduct lapsed - its vault span in the band breached (its chamber collapsing) and a support in the band cleared by V06 §3.19.2 (3) - and, on a second run, the aqueduct deleted by hand: the run whole across each former support and the former vault, at full height beneath each fallen span, the enceinte's closure unchanged and 0 gaps in its band, the delete's undo restoring the abutments and the cap'.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-epoch). A raised way created across a run that is already breached or dismantled. Since R5-02 a crossing station is made only 'where a raised way is created across a standing wall'. Its support 'is the band's stretch under the deck', and it 'carries no state of its own - it reads its stretch's condition, ... breached or dismantled a ruined one' (§2.7's support step (3), base l.2548-2575). The only rule that keeps a deck off a fallen wall is the repair's: 'a repairRaised of a span beside a station whose stretch is breached or dismantled ... first repairs that stretch by repairWall ... so no deck stands on a fallen wall'. S7's generation row maps a breached draw there to worn only because S7 writes conditions after S6's aqueduct. Nothing covers the creation itself. V06 §3.19 (5)'s founding passes the course 'where the course crosses a standing curtain ... through a wall opening ... or a raised gate ... added as S7 furniture in the commit' (V06 l.2824-2826), whatever the run's condition; so do the history replay's founding at generation and a hand aqueduct drawn across a gap (§7.1). Item 114 decays safe, poor or neglected curtains into breached and dismantled runs (T114-3 runs a neglected CITY over 20 epochs). An aqueduct founded later across such a run gets its crossing station on a fallen support at its first commit: a deck standing on nothing, with the clear-span bound read across a station that does not stand. One builder places the station anyway. Another reads a gap as no 'stretch standing' ((d)'s list names 'a dismantled stretch rebuilt on its line' as laid after) and raises an ordinary pier, which (3) slides out of the wall strip. A third repairs the run first.
required_change: §2.7's support step (3), after '(crossings in order along the deck, each taking the nearest interior station not yet taken, ties to the earlier; one added there where none lies within p / 2)', add: '; where the run under that station is breached or dismantled when the raised way is created - an epoch's founding across a decayed curtain (V06 §3.19 (5)), the history replay's, a hand aqueduct drawn across a gap - the creating commit first repairs that stretch by repairWall in the same batch, in item 114's patch material (the row V06 §3.7.7 (3) draws; on a dismantled stretch the op's bend, V06 §2.8: a new stretch drawn on its line), as a repairRaised beside a fallen stretch does (below), so no deck stands on a fallen wall from its first commit, a hand aqueduct's dry run listing the repair as a fate'. Ends: (1) V06: §3.19 (5)'s 'added as S7 furniture in the commit' adds '- a breached or dismantled run at the crossing first repaired by repairWall in that batch, charged to the fabric cap with the founding (§2.7's support step (3))'. (2) scope: §13.2 T114-3 adds 'an aqueduct founded at an epoch across the decayed ring where the run at its crossing is breached, and on a second run dismantled, and a hand aqueduct drawn across such a run: that run repaired in patch material in the creating batch, the station's support standing, never a deck over a gap at any commit, the hand case's undo restoring the gap'. T-V6-73 and V06 §7's T114 row take the epoch case.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-lock). A regeneration with a held raised way: is the crossing station's raised gate re-derived? R5-02 put two sentences into §2.7's support step (6). One: 'A lock or pin holds the same; at a regeneration a locked, pinned or declared raised way stands before every stage the regeneration runs (§7.2)'. The other, its closing sentence (base l.2618-2623): 'at a regeneration the stretches it re-derives are laid after a held raised way (above) - a re-derived stretch on a crossing station's line takes the station into the line as its support again, so an unchanged regeneration reproduces it'. Take a CITY whose S4 timber viaduct crosses S3's ring at a raised gate (T110-2's own fixture), with the viaduct locked, then a full Regenerate (keep). S3's ring is re-derived as a stretch laid after the viaduct. The closing sentence keeps the station as its support - a viaduct's station's support is 'the raised gate, whose tower carries the deck'. But (d) says such a stretch 'takes no crossing station and makes no gate on the deck', and that 'no gate or tower stands in the under-deck strip - one the wall's law would place there moves to the nearest point clear of it'. §4.8 Gates says 'A stretch laid after a raised way takes no crossing furniture' (l.7674-7675), and counts a raised gate only 'where the arterial's raised way was created across the standing trace'. So one builder reproduces the raised gate and N1. Another moves S3's gate out of the under-deck strip, passes the deck over the ring ungated and changes the ring's gates - an unchanged regeneration that does not reproduce. T110-2 (6) runs only 'a Re-derive from S4', which never re-derives S3's ring, so no bar runs the case.
required_change: §2.7's support step (6), closing paragraph: 'a re-derived stretch on a crossing station's line takes the station into the line as its support again, so an unchanged regeneration reproduces it' -> 'a re-derived stretch on a crossing station's line takes the station into the line as its support again with its crossing furniture - a raised gate (the gate law's site there read as that gate, never moved out of the under-deck strip by (d)) or a wall opening (§4.8 Gates) - so an unchanged regeneration reproduces it, its gates and their count included'. Ends: (1) pipeline: §4.8 Gates's 'A stretch laid after a raised way takes no crossing furniture: it runs on beneath the deck, which passes over it with no gate (§2.7's support step (6) (d))' adds '; a stretch a regeneration re-derives on a held raised way's crossing station keeps that station's furniture (§2.7's support step (6))'. (2) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (6) adds 'and a full Regenerate (keep) of the CITY fixture whose S4 timber viaduct crosses S3's ring at a raised gate, that viaduct locked: S3's ring, its N1 gates - the raised gate among them, on its station - and the station's support reproduced byte-identically'.

claim: The round-5 `supports` comment (l. 2292) puts a `state` on a crossing station only once no 'wall stretch lies under it', and the new closing paragraph of (6) (l. 2617-2622) gives the one rule for such a station, inside its regeneration clause: 'a station no stretch lies under any more stands as a pier (its `ring` by (4)), its `supports` entry then carrying its own `state`'. Outside a regeneration the stretch under a crossing station is taken whole after its release (both spans `ruined` or `cleared`, (3)): V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1612-1618) dismantles it 'after `wallToWay` as after `absorbWall`, the fortification loop keeping the record while such a stretch stands'; `wallToWay` (§4.11 l. 8214-8221) spares it only 'while its deck stands', so it becomes ring road; a hand `delete` takes an ordinary run. Nothing states what the station then is - its `state` and that state's writer, its `ring` - nor what a `repairRaised` beside it does: (3) and V06 §3.19.2 (5) re-lay 'that stretch by `repairWall`', whose op targets a standing enceinte record (V06 §2.8, l. 722). A builder generalising the closing sentence raises a standing pier (no `state`) with a (4) rectangle in the ring road `wallToWay` laid on the old line - a support in a way's corridor, the result T110-2 bars; another reads the station as `dismantled` and, by T114-3's regrowth clause (l. 18557-18562: the curtain absorbed, then the aqueduct repaired, 'the stretch re-laid on its line by `repairWall`'s bend'), re-lays the stretch. Reachable on the item-114 history fixtures (a neglected ring absorbed or converted after its aqueduct toppled).
required_change: §2.7's support step (3), after '... it is an ordinary run (§13.2's item-114 group);': 'where that run is then taken whole - the record dropped once nothing of it stands (V06 §3.7.6 (5), after `absorbWall` or `wallToWay`), or the run removed by `wallToWay` or a hand `delete` - the station reads `dismantled` (a ruined support whose stone is gone: no `state` of its own, no pier, its `ring` kept as its place), and a `repairRaised` beside it first re-lays the stretch on its line by `repairWall`'s bend (a `drawWall` on its line, V06 §2.8) as for a `dismantled` stretch (below), or, where a way now lies on that line, raises a pier on the station by (4), slid clear of the way by (3), its key kept;'. The closing paragraph of (6): 'and a station no stretch lies under any more stands as a pier' -> 'and a station whose deck stands and on whose line no re-derived stretch lies stands as a pier'. The `supports` comment: 'never on a crossing station while a wall stretch lies under it, whose `condition` it reads' -> 'never on a crossing station while a wall stretch lies under it, whose `condition` it reads, nor once that stretch is taken whole (it then reads `dismantled`)'. Scope end: §13.2's T114-3 regrowth clause adds a run whose curtain is converted by `wallToWay` after both spans fell - the station read `dismantled`, no support in the ring road, the repair's pier clear of it. (The adjudicator may rule another outcome, provided the station's `state` has one named writer, no support stands in a way's corridor and T114-3's regrowth clause holds.)

claim: §2.7's support step (6) (d) (l. 2607–2609), the home R5-02 wrote this round, makes a wall run laid after a raised way, beneath every non-`vault` span, 'an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit (the arch walled up; derived at read, never stored — §4.5's daylight casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF wall read it)'. Its restatements state a different height: §8.4's heightfield writers (l. 13672–13673) and shadow casters (l. 13897–13898) 'a run beneath a raised way's span topped at its soffit'; §11.1's glTF row (l. 15988) 'topped at that span's soffit' and CityJSON row (l. 15989) 'topped at its soffit as in glTF'; §4.5's casters (l. 6150) 'to its soffit'; §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10631) 'topped at a span's soffit'; T110-2 (4) (l. 18495–18496) and V06 l. 4170 'topped at its soffit'. R5-02's own summary says 'walled up to a span's soffit'. Where a span's soffit stands above the run's own top, the home gives the run its own height with the arch open above it, and the readers give a run raised to the soffit with the arch filled. This is common: a soffit is at least `clearanceCm` (450 cm for carts, V11 l. 702), and an aqueduct's or a valley viaduct's arches are far taller than a curtain wall. Two builders draw and export different walls, shadow prisms and heightfield tops. No bar separates them: T110-2's and V06's '0 wall runs above a span's soffit' passes both. (6) (d)'s reader list also omits CityJSON's wall objects, which §11.1 now makes read it (repair-r5-rendering's HAND-OFF to model).
required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (d): 'beneath every other span it is an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit (the arch walled up; derived at read, never stored — §4.5's daylight casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF wall read it)' → 'beneath every other span it is an ordinary run at its own height, its top cut down to that span's soffit where the soffit is lower — the arch walled up to that top, a run lower than the soffit leaving the arch open above it (derived at read, never stored — §4.5's daylight casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF wall and CityJSON wall objects read it)'. If the adjudicator rules the arch filled to the soffit instead, the home states that for both cases. Each restatement then reads the home's words, citing it. END lines: rendering — §8.4's heightfield writers and shadow casters, and §11.1's glTF and CityJSON clauses, 'a run beneath a raised way's span with its top cut down to that span's soffit where the soffit is lower (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. pipeline — §4.5's casters (l. 6150). determinism — §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10631). scope — T110-2 (4) 'an ordinary run beneath every other span, its top cut down to the span's soffit where the soffit is lower', and its fixture adds 'a span whose soffit stands above the ring's wall top: the run at its own height, the arch open above it'. V06 — l. 4170, in the same words.

claim: ONE FIX WITH VEW-r5-02 (verify-edges-world-r5t), found independently from V06's side. Under R5-02 a wall stretch laid after a raised way is closed against each support, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span in its band, ends at a `vault` span's two walled-up arch mouths, and beneath every other span is a run topped at the soffit, derived at read (§2.7's support step (6) (d), base l. 2603-2614; V06 §3.7.6 (5); T-V6-47; V07 §3.5a (4)). Those parts then go on ordinary paths: V06 §3.19.2 (3)'s salvage `dismantle` clears a support whose spans have fallen (only a crossing station's is spared, and a support a later wall abuts is none), a span's arch-vault chambers collapse with it in the same batch (l. 2932), §3.11.4's `topple` breaks both spans beside a support, and a hand `delete` removes the whole raised way. Nothing says what the wall's line becomes across the former part (a gap, a `breached` run or a run standing whole), nor what height the run has once its span is ruined, cleared or removed. This is reached on H-AQUA itself: its METROPOLIS circuit runs on beneath its aqueduct, which runs dry in year 170, lapses, falls by span and is salvaged.
